summary:
TerraVanguard is a free, multilingual web app that helps farmers explore crop rotation strategies that strengthen soil health and adapt their farms to changing conditions. Farmers draw the exact boundary of their field on a map, and the app automatically retrieves NASA Earth observations for that field. These include climate (POWER, IMERG), soil moisture (SMAP, GLDAS), water stress (ECOSTRESS), vegetation (HLS Landsat/Sentinel-2, MODIS, VIIRS) and terrain (NASADEM). The data are combined with local soil information, crop characteristics and the farmer’s own priorities to build and compare 4-year rotation plans, with irrigation guidance, weather and vegetation alerts, and a PDF report that lists sources and limitations.

This matters because changing temperatures, unpredictable rainfall, water scarcity and declining soil health threaten farms worldwide. Most small and medium farmers lack data for their own field. TerraVanguard turns complex satellite data into practical, field-specific decisions that anyone can use.
details:
What it does and how it works
TerraVanguard is a free, multilingual (full English and Spanish, partial Portuguese and French) web app that helps farmers explore crop rotation strategies that strengthen soil health and adapt to changing conditions.

  1. Draw a field: the farmer draws the exact boundary of their parcel on a map.
  2. Diagnose: the app automatically retrieves NASA Earth observations for that field: climate (NASA POWER, GPM IMERG), soil moisture (SMAP, GLDAS), water and heat stress (ECOSTRESS), vegetation (HLS Landsat/Sentinel-2, MODIS, VIIRS), biomass (GEDI) and terrain (NASADEM).
  3. Plan: a rotation engine combines these observations with local soil information (SoilGrids profiles plus the farmer’s own pH and organic matter tests), crop characteristics (26 crops, FAO GAEZ v5 suitability and FAO-56 crop stages) and farmer priorities (climate scenario, irrigation and strategy). It then builds and compares 4-year rotation plans and perennial planting options. Plans recalculate instantly when the farmer changes an input.
  4. Act and follow up: the app provides daily irrigation guidance using a simplified FAO-56 water balance, a crop calendar, and alerts for frost, heat, heavy rain and NDVI decline. It adds regional context from FIRMS fire detections and GloFAS river forecasts. Farmers also get a private field journal with photos that works offline, a cost and break-even calculator, and a PDF report listing data sources and limitations.

Benefits
Small and medium farmers who lack access to agronomic advice get a field-specific, science-based starting point for their decisions, for free and from any device. Satellite data become plain-language choices: which crop to plant next, how much water it needs, and what risks are coming.

Intended impact
We want to help farmers protect their soil, use water more efficiently and adapt to climate change before losses happen. A farmer in the Peruvian Andes, where we tested the app in the Mantaro Valley, can use the same NASA data as a large research institution. Because the tool is global and bilingual, it can scale to farming communities worldwide.

Creativity

  • Instead of showing raw maps, TerraVanguard connects more than 12 NASA datasets directly to a farming decision: a rotation plan for one specific field.
  • Farmers can add their own soil tests and experiences, so satellite estimates and local knowledge improve each other.
  • The app is transparent about uncertainty. Every result shows its source, date, resolution and quality, and the app explains the difference between a satellite estimate and a field measurement.

Factors we considered

  • Data quality: cloud, shadow and snow masks, quality flags, outdated-data warnings, and detection of disagreement between sources (for example, ERA5 vs. POWER rainfall).
  • Honesty about limits: the soil indicator is orientative context, not a lab diagnosis, and recommendations must be confirmed with local field checks.
  • Accessibility: no installation, a mobile-friendly design, an English/Spanish interface, offline capture and no login required for core features.
  • Privacy and security: private records protected by row-level security, and API secrets kept on the server and never exposed in the browser.

Tools and technologies

  • Front end: HTML, CSS and JavaScript, hosted on Netlify.
  • Back end: Supabase (PostgreSQL, authentication, storage, scheduled monitoring) and Edge Functions written in TypeScript/Deno.
  • Geospatial processing: geotiff.js and proj4.
  • Data access: NASA Earthdata, NASA POWER, ORNL DAAC and GIBS APIs, Open-Meteo (ERA5, GloFAS), ISRIC SoilGrids and FAO GAEZ.
  • AI features: an assistant (gpt-oss-120b) and a photo-based pest check, both via Groq.
  • Testing: Node and Deno test suites.

Source code: https://github.com/Zenks-bot/TerraVanguard.git
